external_entities.name: Duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who uses the dispatch console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.
external_entities.notes: The source uses the plural form 'Duty engineers'.

external_entities.name: Scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: Dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript application used by duty engineers and connected to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it. The console and API are served from different origins; CORS configuration is undocumented.

processes.name: Corporate web host
processes.description: The corporate host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: Dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer; it reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.notes: The API allows cross-origin responses, but the allowed origins and credential setting are undocumented.

processes.name: Schedule importer
processes.description: An hourly importer that pulls and parses the scheduling partner's SOAP XML feed and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The importer presents an API token that was issued when it was built and has not been rotated.

data_stores.name: Dispatch database
data_stores.description: Database holding job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order carries the token or session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token. Protection at rest is undocumented.

data_stores.name: Schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder where the importer writes each downloaded scheduling document.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_stores.notes: The archive is described as a folder on the corporate file store; that does not establish its network placement.

data_stores.name: Corporate file store
data_stores.description: The corporate file store containing the schedule archive folder.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a folder on the corporate file store

data_flows.name: load console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer loads the dispatch console from the corporate web host.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The API answers the console cross-origin. Allowed origins and whether credentials are allowed are undocumented.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Whether the socket uses TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, and whether it rechecks the engineer's session are undocumented.

data_flows.name: read-write database
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads from and writes to the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creator tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: pull planned work
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the scheduling partner's planned-work SOAP feed over HTTPS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: How the partner identifies the importer and how the importer identifies the partner are undocumented.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: write archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: The importer presents an API token that was issued when it was built and has not been rotated since.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers sit and the schedule importer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: Production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company zone holding the live estate and accounts able to move crews or change depot work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: Scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the other company that publishes planned work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The API answers the browser console cross-origin and is configured with CORS.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule importer presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is described as an importer that runs hourly, pulls a feed, parses XML, and posts work orders.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API is internally exposed rather than internet-facing.
assumptions.basis: The API runs in the production control plane, which the source states is not reachable from the internet.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It holds crew names and mobile numbers, as well as creator tokens or sessions.
